definition: A set is a collection of objects, called its elements, usually written inside curly brackets, such as $\{2, 4, 6\}$.
An element is one member of a set; $n(A)$ is the number of elements in set $A$.
The universal set, $\mathscr{E}$, is the set of every element being considered in a question, drawn as the rectangle in a Venn diagram.
The complement of set $A$, written $A'$, is the set of elements of the universal set that are not in $A$.
The union of sets $A$ and $B$, written $A \cup B$, is the set of elements in $A$ or $B$ or both.
The intersection of sets $A$ and $B$, written $A \cap B$, is the set of elements that are in both $A$ and $B$.
A Venn diagram shows the universal set as a rectangle and each set as a circle inside it, with overlaps for elements the sets share.
Set $A$ is a subset of set $B$, written $A \subseteq B$, when every element of $A$ is also an element of $B$.
The empty set, written $\varnothing$ or $\{\,\}$, is the set with no elements.
